# Rules and diagnostics

spec

Rules are grouped like in Biome: syntax, schema, graph, text, markdown, style, trace, build, meta and custom. A code such as DOC301 is a public contract and never changes; retired codes are not reused. Messages are in English and every message has a hint.

The rule schema/missing-kind-schema (DOC109) is an error by default: every document needs a kind with a schema. The rules style/hedging (DOC352) and style/timeless-words (DOC353) warn about vague and time-bound words by default.

The preset recommended gives every rule a default level. Rules that are off by default form the nursery group: they are noisy on Russian text or need a deliberate choice, and are enabled in the configuration, one by one or as a group.

Core rules are always errors and cannot be suppressed or switched off: broken JSON, duplicate keys, a missing title, invalid ids, the built-in schema, duplicate ids, broken references, orphans, parent cycles, missing roots, links to hidden documents, bad includes, unknown ids in code tags and stale output.

Rule levels are set in [Configuration](config.md); the commands that run the rules are in [Commands](commands.md).

## Diagnostic format

Text form: file:line:column: level CODE (group/name) message, followed by a line with the hint, then a summary line such as checked 3 files: 1 error, 0 warnings. JSON form: an envelope with a summary (checked, errors, warnings, shown, truncated) and a diagnostics array of objects with code, rule, level, file, line, column, endLine, endColumn, message, hint and fixable. When the output is cut by max-diagnostics, truncated is true.

The order is deterministic: level, file path, line, column, code, rule name. Columns count Unicode characters of the source text, also inside strings with escape sequences.

## See also

Run docc rules for the list with current levels and docc explain with a code for a description and an example.
